messages.author: 0efd2d7533d4b99f
messages.subject: install seewave on Mac
parts:
Hi all, when trying to install seewave in RStudio (last version with R 3.4) on a Mac with ElCapitan OS, I get this message:

> install.packages("seewave", repos="http://cran.at.r-project.org/")
Package which is only available in source form, and may need compilation of C/C++/Fortran: ‘seewave’
Do you want to attempt to install these from sources?
y/n: 


then if I say Y, I get this:

y/n: y
installing the source package ‘seewave’

provo con l'URL 'http://cran.at.r-project.org/src/contrib/seewave_2.0.5.tar.gz'
Content type 'application/x-gzip' length 2492482 bytes (2.4 MB)
==================================================
downloaded 2.4 MB

* installing *source* package ‘seewave’ ...
** package ‘seewave’ successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** libs


Agreeing to the Xcode/iOS license requires admin privileges, please re-run as root via sudo.


ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘seewave’
* removing ‘/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.4/Resources/library/seewave’
Warning in install.packages :
  installation of package ‘seewave’ had non-zero exit status

The downloaded source packages are in
‘/private/var/folders/b7/15lcyj4j4n13bbs8q79_x5br0000gn/T/RtmplXKMXb/downloaded_packages’
> 


Any hint on how to solve this problem ?

Gianni

messages.author: bfa183f4897a5619
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] install seewave on Mac
parts:
Hi Gianni,

I suspect that the requirement for root may have to do with XCode rather than seewave proper. The C and Fortran compilers on Macs are part of the XCode package, and you need to agree to that package's license agreement before you can use the compilers.

I believe that if you search for xcode in spotlight, open it up, and agree to the licensing stuff, the seewave compile should run fine without root.

best,
jesse
